Marissa — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. Quick prelim analysis based on FinArc's request ids and our sidecar traces: this looks like autoscaler-driven cold boots where GPU inference instances are being created from standby. The p99 spikes coincide with first-token kernel JIT / cuBLAS initialization and KV cache miss storms when many concurrent sessions start.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked by speed to deploy):
1) Account-level change: increase min_reserved_instances for FinArc from 0 to 2 for the next 6 hours (keeps two warm GPUs available). Low risk; will incur additional cost for them. Can be reverted after the peak window.
2) Enable "steady-warm" policy for their hosted model route: keep N warm replicas and allow fast warm-path (we already have this as a feature toggle). Needs ops flip but no code change for the customer.
3) Short-term routing: failover to our quantized CPU variant for non-latency-sensitive paths while the GPU pool warms. This sacrifices tail latency for throughput on specific routes.

We can also push a runtime patch to pre-warm kernels during instance spinup (takes ~2–3 days for safe rollout). Logs attached: engineer_prelim_logs_snippet.txt shows the timestamps and the kernel-init stack.

I'll apply option (1) immediately if we get approval from ops/finance and a note to the customer offering to cover the incremental cost for the 6-hour window as a courtesy.
